## Paper

## Abstract

The African large low shear wave-velocity province (LLSVP) advected plumes manifest as large igneous provinces (LIPs) during Pangea breakup. The existence of such basal mantle structures during earlier supercontinents is unknown. Here we analyze samples from China and Brazil to demonstrate with literature data a series of seven LIPs of supercontinent Rodinia from 940–720 million years ago. Multi-proxy reconstruction results in a coherent ring of LIPs comparable with the size of Rodinia that resembles the product of an ancient LLSVP whose edges advected LIP-producing plumes. Oceanic lithosphere recycling following supercontinental assembly is evident in Nd isotopes as evolving LIP-sources. There is a same secular variational pattern of LIP sources with a replenished depleted component advected by plumes as well as a similar manner yet contrasting paleogeographic configurations corresponding to supercontinental breakup between Rodinian and Pangean LLSVPs. This evolving pattern of LLSVPs suggests their partial regeneration (replenishment and migration) between supercontinents.

---

## Introduction

Large low shear wave velocity provinces (LLSVPs) in the lowermost mantle imaged seismically 1–3 represent the largest geophysical/geological structures on the planet. Although imaged only at the present-day, LLSVPs exhibit correlations with geological data that suggest the basal mantle structures could be quite ancient. The configuration of such historical basal mantle structures reveals a close but enigmatic relationship between LLSVPs and supercontinents 4. As such, LLSVPs have the potential for informing the geodynamic–tectonic coupling of historical supercontinent cycles, as well as the prediction of a future supercontinent 5,6. At present, Earth has two antipodal and equatorial LLSVPs that reflect the dominance of degree-2 mantle convection 2,3.

LIPs occurring in the Pacific Ocean including ocean plateaus are well-documented to correlate with the Pacific LLSVP with significant interaction between plumes and mid-ocean ridges in pulses separated by ~10–20 million years (Myr, ref. 7). The present African (hereafter ‘Pangean’ to name the historic one during the Pangea tenure) LLSVP is thought to have been responsible for the breakup of the Pangea supercontinent, which lasted for 200 Myr accompanied by six major large igneous provinces (LIPs)/plumes 8–12 (Fig. 1). It has been revealed that all these LIPs systematically occurred within or along the edges (within ~10˚; ref. 13.) of the Pangean LLSVP and have thus arguably been advected by it 10,14 (Fig. 1). It therefore begs the question whether Pangea’s predecessor also had a LLSVP beneath it, and reconstructing the LIPs that might have emanated from it is an obvious test of its existence. In addition, beyond a certain age, which is debated, the formation 15–17 and the fixity 18,19 or mobility 20–22 of the present LLSVP is unknown, yet critical for understanding geodynamic–tectonic coupling.

In this study, building of the empirical and theoretical correspondences among a supercontinent, its LIPs, and its underlying LLSVP, we attempt to identify a hypothetical LLSVP underlying Neoproterozoic supercontinent Rodinia using its LIPs and to decipher its formation by comparing it with that of the Pangea (Fig. 1). Datasets of the geochronology and geochemistry of the global Rodinian LIPs—in total, 22 elements (Fig. 2)—are compiled, among them the ca. 920 Ma and ca. 820 Ma LIPs are updated with analyzed data (Methods; Supplementary Data 1–4; literature data from Supplementary References). The geometries of all these LIPs are reconstructed based on a synthesis configuration of Rodinia 23,24 in order to assess their possible corresponding basal mantle structure during the evolution of the Neoproterozoic supercontinent; while the secular variations of geochemical proxies of the Rodinian LIPs, as well as their comparison with the Pangean LIPs and LIPs during the supercontinental assembly and tenure, are analyzed to constrain the evolution of this basal mantle structure (Methods).

---

## Results

Chemical evolution of global 940–720 Ma (Rodinian) LIPs

Vestiges of each Rodinian LIP are internally consistent in chemistry and all the LIPs have an affinity of continental flood basalts, referring a plume-origin (Methods). Comparing the seven Rodinian LIPs, there are both notable similarities and systematic changes over time. The εNdt values exhibit dominantly chondritic-like values, though there is an increase of diversified features with younging direction (Fig. 3). This commonality may indicate a similar dominant source for the seven LIPs, one which was extracted from primitive mantle as chondrite-like (primordial) source(s), and the cumulative decay of Sm through time hardly changed their εNdt values. However, they also show a transition from initially narrow values that evolve over time into a fanning isotopic array toward both more enriched and depleted εNdt values (Fig. 3). This observation may suggest an increasing contribution of depleted (mantle) source(s) on one hand, and a simultaneous increasing contribution of enriched source (Nd TDM > 1700 Ma) on the other. For instance, among the seven LIPs, the ca. 720 Ma LIP shows the widest span of εNd values (Fig. 3), which may indicate the largest contributions of ancient lithosphere while simultaneously also the largest contribution of depleted mantle, both in addition to the primordial source. There are systematic changes of chemical proxies in the LIP compositions over time: The decreasing of Gd/Yb n while the elevated Mg-numbers, Ni-contents, and Nb/Ta ratios over time might indicate increasing influences of depleted source with depleted compatible elements 25 in the primordial magmas (Fig. 3) (Methods). In summary, the Rodinian LIPs exhibit an increasing geochemical diversity with increasing contributions from both enriched and depleted sources over time, a compositional pattern similar to that of the Pangean (Fig. 3).

Reconstruction of Rodinian LIPs

Seven Rodinian LIP episodes are classified, i.e., ca. 940 Ma Göteborg-Baengnyeong, ca. 920 Ma Dashigou–Gangila, ca. 890 Ma Iguerda–Sariwon, ca. 820 Ma Willouran-Qianlishan, ca. 780 Ma Gunbarrel, and ca. 720 Ma Franklin (Fig. 2), which are consistent with the peaks in the probability histogram of all available ages of the global LIP vestiges (Fig. 1). It is well-known that the pinpoint of a giant dike swarm of a LIP estimates its plume center 26,27. Here, all the coeval units of a potential LIP are correlated to estimate its magma center close to breakup margins based on the paleogeographic reconstruction in the framework of the Rodinia supercontinent. Two prevailing reconstructions of Rodinia by Evans 23 (Fig. 4a) and Li, et al. 24 (Fig. 4b) are applied. Both options successfully reconstruct most LIPs, but do not support the correlation of all the others as an intact LIP at each stage. To construct as many associated units to a same LIP center as possible, a few cratons including North China 28 and Tarim 29 during 940–760 Ma and South China 24,30 during 820–720 Ma are relocated based on alternative possibilities based on the configuration of Evans 23 (Fig. 4c), which constructs all vestiges of 940–720 Ma LIPs from different blocks into intact LIPs of each time, compatible with the available paleomagnetic data. The three models yield slightly different spatial distributions of plume centers and LIPs; yet they all show three major break-up stages, i.e., São Francisco–Congo and West Africa during 940–890 Ma, Indian and Australia-East Antarctic during 820–760 Ma, and finally Siberia at ca. 720 Ma (Fig. 4d–f).

---

## Methods

Geochronologic and geochemical analyses

Fresh samples were obtained from the ca. 920 Ma (Dashigou and Bahia dike swarms) and ca. 820 Ma (Luanchuan sill complex) LIP vestiges in the North China and São Francisco-Congo cratons. The information of the samples are provided (Fig. 2; Supplementary Data 1; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2).

Bulk whole-rock elements and Nd–Sr isotopes of some representative samples are analyzed in the Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IGGCAS, Beijing). Major element determinations are performed by X-ray fluorescence and the precisions are better than 0.2 wt% in the analyzable ranges. Trace element analyses are determined using inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and the relative standard deviation was better than 5% above the detective limit. Sr–Nd isotope determination is made by ICP-MS, and the procedure backgrounds for Sr–Nd isotope analyses were better than 50 pg, and the external precision (2σ) of 147Sm/144Nd ratios was better than 0.5%. All the generated data are compiled together with global datasets (Supplementary Data 2 and 3) and plotted together (Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4).

Baddeleyite (ZrO 2 ) grains are liberated from coarse samples. The minerals are then mounted in an epoxy resin and their U–Pb isotopic ratios are analyzed using a multi-collector CAMECA 1280 IMS facility in the IGGCAS. The diameter of the ion beam for analyses is ~20 μm. During data processing, an average of present-day crustal composition is used for common Pb correction, and the weighted means are given at 2σ (Supplementary Data 4). Analytical procedures and data processing follow those described in ref. 59.

Application of geochemical proxies (Mg number, Ni content, Gd/Yb n , 87Sr/86Srt, εNdt, and Nd T DM age)

Here a few geochemical proxies of whole-rock compositions are applied. Among them, Mg number is calculated as Mg/(Mg+Fe) in molecular; while Gd/Yb n is Gd/Yb ratio of a rock normalized to chondrite. Due to the different compatibility of elements between melts and minerals (mantle source) 60,61, Mg numbers, Ni contents and Nb/Ta ratios are relatively higher in melts with higher degrees of melting from a same source, and melts from relatively more depleted sources 25,62 may show relatively higher of these values; while Gd/Yb n values are on the contrary. In addition, crustal rocks/melts have much lower Mg numbers, Ni contents and Nb/Ta ratios but distinct higher Gd/Yb n values 63. It should be also mentioned that these values/ratios can be decreased in the magma when a fractionating phase is compatible with the proxies.

87Sr/86Srt, εNdt and Nd T DM ages are calculated (Supplementary Data 3):

87Sr/86Srt = 87Sr/86Sr - 87Rb/86Sr × (eλtage - 1)

Where λ = 1.42 × 10-11 Myr-1.

εNdt = 10000 × [ (143Nd/144Nd sample, measured - (147Sm/144Nd sample, measured) × (eλtage, Ma - 1)) / (143Nd/144Nd CHUR, 0 - (147Sm/144Nd CHUR, 0 × (eλtage, Ma - 1)) - 1 ]

Nd T DM age = (1/λ) × ln( (143Nd/144Nd sample - 143Nd/144Nd DM) / (147Sm/144Nd sample - 147Sm/144Nd DM) + 1 )

Where 143Nd/144Nd CHUR, 0 = 0.512638, 147Sm/144Nd CHUR, 0 = 0.1967; 143Nd/144Nd DM = 0.51315; 147Sm/144Nd DM = 0.2137, and λ = 6.54 × 10-12 Myr-1.

Here 87Sr/86Srt refers to 87Sr/86Sr of an igneous rock at the time of its crystallization while εNdt 64 refers to 143Nd/144Nd at the time of crystallization normalized to that of chondrite. Both proxies indicate the nature of source of an igneous rock which it crystalizes. In a close system, the 87Sr/86Sr (143Nd/144Nd) of a rock/source region increases due to the decay of 87Rb to 87Sr (147Sm to 143Nd); and the higher the Rb/Sr (Sm/Nd), the more prominent the increase. In addition, if 147Sm/144Nd is lower (higher) than a chondrite value (0.1976), εNdt decrease (increase) (Fig. 3). Nd T DM age 62 refers to the age assuming an igneous rock derived from the secular depleted mantle after the historical derivation of lithosphere.

Discrimination of ancient large igneous provinces (LIPs) with plume origin and reconstruction of their plume centers

LIPs comprise large volumes of mafic rocks, represented by flood basalts; however, many of them were eroded, leaving vestiges of mainly their plumbing system represented by the dike swarms, and dispersed during continental breakup 65,66. Consequently, LIP elements with similar high-precision ages (e.g., baddeleyite U-Pb ages) were possibly dispersed from a historically same LIP, if they can be tested by associated compositions and paleogeographic reconstructions (e.g., close to each other enough in a paleogeographic model). LIPs are characterized by igneous pulse of short duration (~1–5 Myr) with a maximum lifespan of ~50 Myr 67. The associated compositions are represented by consistent patterns in the chondrite- and primitive mantle-normalized trace element spidergrams (Supplementary Fig. 3), as well as closely distributed Sr-Nd isotopes for samples of the same swarm (Supplementary Fig. 4a). All the global ca. 940–720 Ma LIP elements are collected (Supplementary Data 1), which are mostly summarized in www.largeigneousprovince.org and documented previously 68–72 but here in the ca. 920 Ma and ca. 820 Ma LIP elements are updated to give better constraints on the global paleogeographic reconstruction at these two very periods. Here we arbitrary take 20 Myr as a kind of threshold as all the age data of LIP vestiges of 940–720 Ma LIP elements show different peaks with widths of within 20 Ma (Fig. 1) and as many of these ages have errors range from 1 to 10 Ma irrespectively of systematic errors induced by different labs (Supplementary Data 1); and thus this age threshold is rather an age uncertainty than durations of events. Based on the compiled datasets and data reported here, totally seven LIPs are defined: i.e., ca. 940 Ma Göteborg–Baengnyoeng LIP (with dismembered elements in Baltic and North China) 73–75, the ca. 920 Ma Dashigou–Gangila LIP (with elements in North China, São Francisco–Congo, and West Africa) 72,76,77, the ca. 890 Ma Iguerda–Taïfast LIP (with elements in North China, West Africa, and Tarim) 75,77–80, the ca. 820 Ma Willouran–Guibei LIP (with elements in South Australia, South China, Tarim, and North China) 81–84, the ca. 780 Ma Gunbarrel–Yanbian LIP (with elements in Laurentia, South Australia, South China, and West Australia) 68–70,85–87, ca. 760 Ma Mundine Well LIP (with elements in South Australia, Laurentia, and India) 68–70,85–87, and the ca. 720 Ma Franklin LIP (with elements in Laurentia, Greenland, Siberia, and South China) 71,88–90 (Fig. 2). Each generation of LIP vestiges shows consistent trace element patterns, and most of them show similar trace element patterns akin to ocean island basalt and global LIPs/continental flood basalt, or around two patterns (Supplementary Fig. 3). Such an affinity is consistent with those of the products of mantle plumes 91. Their Sr-Nd isotopes plot mostly along the mantle array and close to the chondrite line, varying from prevalent mantle and enriched mantle; while the TiO 2 /Yb versus Th/Nb diagram 92 shows a feature of plume array with varied degrees of lithospheric input (Supplementary Fig. 4a, b). This agrees with the result of broad studies that the Rodinia has been invoked in the advection of multiple plumes during 940–720 Ma, leading to the diachronous breakup of the supercontinent 68,72–80.

Giant radiate dike swarms are typical magma plumbing systems of LIPs produced by plumes 26,27; consequently, coeval fossil units of a potential LIP can be correlated to estimate its magma center along the breakup margins, as well as the pinpoint of the dike swarm. Due to a complicate situation of preservation, as well as post-emplacement breakup, the original radiating dike swarm may present as dismembered fossil units. The plume centers of the above seven LIPs are reconstructed by join vestiges of a same LIP as many as possible, and geographically neighboring as close as possible, using different reconstructions of global continents (Fig. 4c). The two key LIPs (920 Ma and 820 Ma) with substantial updates and definition, are specified below.

Reconstruction of the 920 Ma LIP: Vestiges of the ca. 920 Ma LIP have been identified on two cratons, including the Dashigou dike swarm 93 and associated sill complexes near the magmatic center (rift) 94 in the North China craton, and the Bahia-Gangila-Mayumbian dike swarm and the associated sill complexes, volcanics, and plutons in the São Francisco craton 72 (Fig. 2; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2). The ca. 920 Ma dikes of both cratons are generally wide (10–50 m) and gabbroic to doleritic 72,93; and the sills are generally thick (100–150 m) and show highly differentiated layers (including syenitic and high-Fe-Ti gabbroic layers) 94. Matching trace element patterns (Supplementary Fig. 3) of the two swarms specifically represented by the two dikes support the hypothesis that these vestiges were part of the same, since dismembered LIP 72,93. Here one baddeleyite sample from a ~50-m-wide, 315˚-trending doleritic dike from the Dashigou swarm of North China give a 207Pb/206Pb age of 918 ± 4 Ma (MSWD = 1.3; n = 14), which is within error the same with the other from a ~40-m-wide 285˚-trending doleritic dike from the Bahia dike swarm of São Francisco (207Pb/206Pb age, 914 ± 8 Ma, MSWD = 0.6; n = 8) (Supplementary Fig. 2). The consistence with reported data (Supplementary Data 1) negates intra-laboratory systematic error and verifies the contemporaneous of the two swarms. It has been proposed the magma center of the Dashigou units was located at the present southeast margin of North China in the Xuhuai rift 94, while that of the Bahia–Gangila–Mayumbian units was located at the present southeast margin of São Francisco in the Macaúbas basin 72 (Supplementary Fig. 1). To reconstruct these units as a contiguous LIP, the magma/rift centers of the two associated cratonic margins should have been conjugate margins and be as closely positioned as possible. The εNdt values of the rocks vary from −2.0 to +3.0 and 87Sr/86Srt vary between 0.702–0.710, and are close to the prevalent mantle (PREMA) (Supplementary Fig. 4a). They have bimodal compositions 94, enriched light rare earth elements, and minor depletion in high-field strength elements compared with the neighboring large-ion lithophile elements, which match that of continental flood basalt and is close to those of oceanic island basalt (Supplementary Fig. 3) and show a mixing trend between plume and lithosphere (Fig. 3) 92.

Reconstruction of the 820 Ma LIP: Vestiges of the ca. 820 Ma LIP have been reported from Gawler (South Australia) as represented by the Willouran (Gairdner) dike swarm and volcanic province 81, South China as represented by the Guibei volcanic-dominated igneous province (with minor dikes) 81,82, and Tarim as represented by the Aksu dike swarm 84. There are also contemporaneous components in North China, including the Qianlishan dike swarm 95, the Jinchuan ultramafic-mafic intrusions (hosting a world-class Ni-Cu deposit) 96, and the bimodal Langshan volcanics 97 along the western margin, and the Luanchuan bimodal sill complex 98 along the southern margin (Fig. 2; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2). The dikes of this event exhibit variable widths (several to tens of meters) and are generally doleritic, with some varieties such as picrite, gabbro, and syenite 81,82,95. These igneous units along the southern and western margins of North China show similar features, e.g., bimodal compositions (mafic/gabbro and felsic/granosyenite) and similar geochemical patterns and Nd-Sr isotopes (Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4a). They are proposed as vestiges of the 820 Ma LIP. Except some volcanics with scattered lithophile-affinitive elements (e.g., the Bikou volcanics in South China), most rocks in North China, Tarim, South China, and South Australia are typically rich in Ba (up to 5000 ppm) (Supplementary Data 2). Their variation from depleted to enriched in Sr and Eu, the largest among the seven LIPs (Supplementary Fig. 3), is consistent with their large lithological variation (from picrite to syenogranite), indicating considerable fractionation, which is further supported by the largely varied contents of compatible elements, such as Ni (Fig. 3). Such similar features among rocks from four different cratons also supports the hypothesis that they are parts of a dismembered LIP. These correlative vestiges of the same LIP indicate magma centers at the present western margins of North China and Tarim and the southeastern and southwestern margins of South Australia and South China, respectively (Fig. 4). The εNdt values of the rocks vary from −7 to +4.5 and 87Sr/86Srt vary between 0.702–0.708: They are close to ocean island basalt, but also showing a transitional feature of melts from prevalent mantle and enriched mantle (Supplementary Fig. 4a). They have bimodal compositions 95, enriched light rare earth elements, and minor depletion in high-field strength elements compared with the neighboring large-ion lithophile elements, which match that of continental flood basalt and ocean island basalt (Supplementary Fig. 3) and show a mixing trend between plume and lithosphere 92.
